title: Typed streaming schema adapters and backward-compatible hydration helpers for Python SDK
creator: Ava Park
description:
Goal: Provide a small, ergonomic compatibility layer and set of helpers for the Python SDK that make it easy for application engineers to consume streaming LLM outputs as typed models (dataclasses and pydantic) while preserving safe retry semantics and supporting schema evolution for backward compatibility.

Background: We have many customers writing parsers that turn dict-based streaming events into domain objects. These parsers often break on model output changes (variants in discriminators, missing fields, added metadata), and are brittle across retries where partial chunks can be re-delivered. This ticket proposes a unified helper package that: (1) offers discriminated union adapters for streamed events, (2) checkpointed hydration for idempotent retries, and (3) stable migration shims for fields renames/optionalization.

Proposed design:
- Provide StreamAdapter base that accepts a small schema descriptor (dataclass or pydantic class) plus a discriminator mapping (token_name -> variant class).
- Support chunked assembly API: adapter.append_chunk(chunk_text, token_index) -> optional hydrated object when assembly completes. The assembly preserves chunk provenance for replay and deduping.
- Checkpointing: expose a compact checkpoint token (opaque string) representing partial assembly state; SDK retry paths can pass the checkpoint to the server and the adapter can resume without double-hydration.
- Backcompat shims: lightweight field-mapping layer and deprecation rules (rename map, defaulting strategies, legacy-variant aliases) that run before final model instantiation.
- Validation & errors: configurable strict/lenient modes. In lenient mode unknown fields are attached to ._meta on the model for observability.

API sketches (user-facing):
- from redwood_sdk.typed_stream import StreamAdapter, register_variant
- adapter = StreamAdapter(schema=MessageV2, discriminator_field=\"kind\", variant_map={\"reply\": ReplyV2, \"edit\": EditV2})
- checkpoint = None
- for chunk in stream: obj = adapter.append_chunk(chunk, checkpoint=checkpoint); if obj: handle(obj)

Acceptance criteria:
- Library implements checkpoint token generation and resume semantics with unit tests that simulate duplicate/reordered chunks.
- Provide migration shim that maps old field names (\"text_body\") to new ones (\"content\") for backwards compatibility and a test demonstrating it.
- Example notebook and short sample app showing dataclass+pydantic usage (one of each) and how to enable lenient mode to capture unknown fields.
- Integration tests against python-sdk streaming harness and a manual runbook for rollout.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for chunk reassembly, checkpoint resume, and variant discrimination.
- Fuzz test harness that injects truncated and duplicated chunks.
- End-to-end test using staging runtime that simulates retries and verifies exactly-once hydration semantics in our consumer shim.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge library behind feature flag in python-sdk (internal alpha).
2) Run staged dogfooding with Solutions and two pilot customers (Backend team to instrument).
3) Collect metrics: hydration error rate, unknown-field rate, and downstream application exceptions.
4) Promote to GA and add examples to SDK docs and quickstart.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Do we support both dataclass and pydantic with a single adapter implementation or provide two thin adapters? (We prefer single adapter with small internal branching for lower maintenance; additional complexity in validation semantics.)
- Checkpoint token size vs fidelity: compact tokens are nicer for network hops but may require more complex encoding. Start with base64-encoded JSON + HMAC and evaluate.

Migration notes:
- Backcompat rules will be opt-in via adapter config until GA. We will provide a CLI inspector to generate suggested rename maps by comparing sample outputs to new schema.

Documentation and artifacts: see links below for design doc, RFC, and example PRs.
